- If sentiment is strongly bullish (≥ 0.67) in recent days, model tends to underreact — increase forecast slightly to align with sentiment momentum.  
- If sentiment is bearish (≤ 0.33) and price is trending up, model often overcorrects — reduce forecast slope to avoid overshoot.  
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >10% from prior peak), model frequently overestimates continuation — cap forecast growth to 5–7% per period.  
- When sentiment shifts from bullish to bearish mid-period, model often fails to adjust — apply a “mean reversion” correction: reduce forecast by 1–2% per period until sentiment stabilizes.  
- If model forecast is flat or trending down while sentiment is bullish, reverse direction slightly — forecast should rise at least 1–2% to match sentiment.  
- For 30-day horizon, model consistently underestimates true price peaks — add 2–3% buffer to forecast if recent sentiment is positive.  
- If sentiment is neutral or mixed (0.33–0.67), model often overfits to recent history — use 3-period moving average to smooth forecast.
